node.label: David R. Roediger
node.date_label: The Wages of Whiteness (1991) · Colored White (2002) · Working Toward Whiteness (2005)
node.description: A labour historian who studies the historical making of whiteness and its consequences for worker solidarity. His interview explicitly acknowledges Du Bois and relates emancipation to a broader history of labour freedom without claiming race explains all working-class conservatism.

proposed_edges.relationship: Relates emancipation and the eight-hour movement to broader struggles over labour freedom.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview credits Du Bois’s general-strike interpretation; no claim that emancipation mechanically caused every later labour development.

proposed_edges.relationship: Examines white-worker identity as historically constructed and as a constraint on class solidarity.
proposed_edges.evidence_note: Own interview distinguishes historical racialization from natural race and explicitly denies race explains everything about labour conservatism.
